title: Orbital roof intradiploic meningioma in a 16-year-old girl
case_prompt:
A 16-year-old girl presented with 2 years of progressive right-eye proptosis and intermittent mild to moderate headache. She denied visual loss or diplopia. Examination showed axial proptosis of the right eye with full extraocular movements. Visual acuity was 6/6 bilaterally, visual fields and funduscopic exam were normal, and the neurologic examination was otherwise unremarkable. Routine hematologic and biochemical tests were normal.  
Orbital CT with thin cuts revealed a 4 × 5 cm hyperdense lesion in the right orbital roof, causing splaying of the inner and outer tables of the skull, enlargement of the orbit, and anterior-medial displacement of the globe. The lesion extended medially to the olfactory groove and posteriorly to the planum sphenoidale, encroached on the ethmoid, sphenoid, and frontal sinuses without bony destruction, and showed slight hyperostosis of the anterior and lateral orbital roof. After contrast, it enhanced homogeneously and intensely.  
MRI demonstrated an iso- to hypointense mass on T1-weighted images and a heterogeneous signal on T2-weighted images at the right orbital roof, with intense enhancement after gadolinium administration.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Fibrous dysplasia considered because of hyperostosis: “the osteoblastic variety causes hyperostosis, which may mimic fibrous dysplasia.”  
2. Solitary osteoma considered because of bone overgrowth: “…the osteoblastic variety causes hyperostosis, which may mimic… solitary osteoma.”  
3. Intraorbital meningioma considered but unlikely since: “intraorbital meningioma presents with proptosis and decline in visual acuity to almost complete vision loss.”  
4. Chondrosarcoma considered but less likely given the absence of aggressive features: “Rarely rapidly progressing chondrosarcoma… is known for aggressive behavior with a high recurrence rate and causes distant metastasis.”  
5. Malignant (osteolytic) intradiploic meningioma considered less likely because: “radiologically intradiploic meningiomas are typically either osteoplastic or osteolytic… the majority are osteoblastic.”  
6. Radiographic features support meningioma given the homogeneous contrast enhancement: “The lesion enhanced homogenously intense after contrast administration.”
